chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: The band's loyalty and Rozelle Claxton's ultimatum
summary: The men say they will follow him back home; Rozelle Claxton says he will take Eddie South's offer if the band leaves.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And so I went on and I talked to the guys about it and as I told you, Chief had tried out with the band, and there's nothing that would do he, he had to leave town with us; so you know, the reputation has been known that bands come from the midwest or west or south, or anywhere, they're known to break up in New York City, and the first thing the guys were telling me is you're going back home with more than you came here with, we're with you, let's go on back, and when Alexander comes up with
something, we'll come back. So I said, you heard what Count said, out of sight, out of mind in a way of speaking. If he comes up with anything, I think we better go.

So I thought and I thought, but then it just kind of worked on me, that they said we're with you; if you stay here, there's one man that spoke up--Rozelle Claxton--that had taken Homer's place, said, Ernie, as long as we can eat, I'm going to be here with you, but if you're going back to Oklahoma, I'm going on and hustling me another job, because I gotta go where the money is.

Now, Eddie South had been begging him to join him, a hundred and fifty dollars a week and lodging, doing nothing but playing the white hotels; he says he told him no, I'm with Ernie Fields band, but if you're all going back to Oklahoma, I'm going to tell him I'll accept it. He said now, if any other dates come on, you make up your mind, I'm with you as long as you're here, I'm not going to let you down, but
